_comment: Synthetic layout-drift fixtures: manifest AND goldens for
scripts/tests/layout_synthetic_test.py and layout_ordering_test.py.
Layout drift is the one thing in this harness that can be SYNTHESIZED with
known ground truth, so unlike every other metric here its correctness is
checkable rather than merely plausible. Each variant renders the SAME body
(body.typ) with one property changed, and declares which drift_classes must
and must not fire.
`overrides` is appended after `base_preamble`; later #set / #let wins in
Typst, so a variant states only what it changes.
kind:
legit       - a difference a converter must be FORGIVEN for. No LAYOUT
class may fire on any of these. This set is the negative
control for every real variant.
real        - drift a converter must be CAUGHT for.
known_blind - real drift this tier provably CANNOT see. Asserted as
invisible so the blind spot is documented rather than
assumed away -- and so that if a future change makes it
visible, this test fails and tells us to promote it.
Goldens are named properties, never numbers: `must_fire` must all fire,
`must_not_fire` must none fire, anything unlisted is don't-care. Listing
every class on every variant would be exactly the over-specification that
makes a golden suite churn.
base_preamble: [A. Author and B. Author. #emph[On the measurement of layout drift]. Journal of Typography, 2021.],
[C. Author. #emph[Content-anchored comparison of rendered documents]. Proc. Fidelity, 2022.],
[D. Author. #emph[Structural similarity considered harmful]. Trans. Metrics, 2023.],
[E. Author and F. Author. #emph[Geometric profiles for cross-engine comparison]. Comput. Doc., 2024.],
[G. Author. #emph[Tolerance design for rendered output]. Softw. Test. Verif., 2020.],
[H. Author and I. Author. #emph[Against pixel registration]. Digit. Publ., 2019.],

variants.name: font_fam
variants.why: a different font family is unavoidable across engines

variants.name: just
variants.why: justified vs ragged-right is a paragraph-breaker difference, not drift

variants.name: size1pt
variants.why: half-point body-size drift is within what class detection can resolve

variants.name: hyphenate_off
variants.why: hyphenation policy differs between engines by default

variants.name: bib_style
variants.why: reference label style is a bibliography choice, not layout drift

variants.name: different_words
variants.why: CONTROL 4 (orthogonality): identical layout, different words. Every layout property must stay within floor while the content tier craters. If a layout metric moves here, it is secretly a text metric.

variants.name: shift1cm
variants.why: CONTROL 5 (orthogonality): the text block moves 1cm right at constant width. Geometry must fire, content must not.

variants.name: twocol
variants.why: 1 column collapses to 2 -- the case mean_ssim scores ABOVE a benign font swap (0.602 vs 0.543)

variants.name: lead
variants.why: leading loosened; the property that drifts in 58/64 corpus papers

variants.name: page_letter
variants.why: A4 -> US Letter; the paper size itself changed

variants.name: small_tier_flattened
variants.why: reproduces the LIVE converter bug: \small / \footnotesize flattened into the body size. Every other property is untouched, which is exactly why no pre-existing metric sees it.

variants.name: dup_block
variants.why: a paragraph emitted twice -- content DUPLICATION, which lowers precision while leaving recall at 1.0. word_recall is a set() and cannot see this at all. small_tier is deliberately NOT in must_not_fire: adding 120 words of body text genuinely dilutes the small-tier share (measured -0.032), which is a true consequence rather than a misattribution. The geometry classes ARE listed, because duplicating content must not move a margin.

variants.name: shuffle_bib
variants.why: the reference list is emitted in reverse order. word_recall is a set() and scores this 1.000.

variants.name: drop_figure
variants.why: A dropped figure is real, serious drift that this tier CANNOT see. extract_spans() reads TEXT spans only, so a vector figure contributes nothing to any geometric property, and losing its caption moves ordered_recall by ~1% -- far under any defensible floor. Documented rather than papered over. Figure COUNT is covered separately by visual_test.py's source_float_counts, and the fix path here is to include page.get_drawings() bboxes in layout_ink_ratio. If this variant ever starts firing, this test fails on purpose: the blind spot closed and the golden should be promoted to kind: real.
